title: Boss: The Hotel Model
summary: Model a small hotel: keys, owned values, conversions, indexes and constraints together.

steps.title: The hotel
steps.body: A hotel needs rooms and guests, modelled carefully: the database should refuse nonsense on its own. Each step adds to your model, so keep everything you wrote: each solution is the whole program so far.

steps.title: Rooms
prompt: Write `enum RoomKind { Single, Double, Suite }`, a `Room` entity and a `HotelDb` context (`Data Source=hotel.db`, `DbSet<Room> Rooms`).
- `int NightlyCents`, which must be greater than 0 (check constraint `CK_Rooms_Price`: `"NightlyCents" > 0`)
Index `(Floor, Kind)` so the front desk can find free rooms on a floor quickly.
solution: protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=hotel.db");
template: Dojo.Check("Number is the key", dojoSql.Contains("\"Number\" TEXT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT \"PK_Rooms\" PRIMARY KEY"), dojoSql);
Dojo.Check("Kind is stored as text", dojoSql.Contains("\"Kind\" TEXT NOT NULL"), dojoSql);
Dojo.Check("(Floor, Kind) is indexed", dojoSql.Contains("(\"Floor\", \"Kind\")"), dojoSql);
dojoDb.Rooms.Add(new Room { Number = "101", Kind = RoomKind.Double, Floor = 1, NightlyCents = 9000 });
dojoDb.Rooms.Add(new Room { Number = "102", Kind = RoomKind.Single, Floor = 1, NightlyCents = 0 });
Dojo.Throws<DbUpdateException>("a free room is refused", () => dojoDb.SaveChanges());

steps.title: Guests
prompt: Add a `Guest` entity (`DbSet<Guest> Guests`) to your context:
- `Address Home`, an **owned** type with `string Street`, `string City` and `string Country`
- `List<string> Allergies`, stored in one text column as a `;`-separated list (`"nuts;milk"`, empty string for none)
Keep everything from the rooms step.
starter: protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=hotel.db");
solution: public Address Home { get; set; } = new();
protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=hotel.db");
template: Dojo.Check("Home is owned (Home_City column)", dojoSql.Contains("\"Home_City\" TEXT NOT NULL"), dojoSql);
Dojo.Check("Email is unique", dojoSql.Contains("CREATE UNIQUE INDEX") && dojoSql.Contains("(\"Email\")"), dojoSql);
Dojo.Eq("Name has a maximum length of 100", 100, dojoDb.Model.FindEntityType(typeof(Guest))?.FindProperty("Name")?.GetMaxLength());
var dojoGuest = new Guest { Name = "Ana", Email = "ana@example.com", Home = new Address { Street = "1 Main St", City = "Kampala", Country = "UG" }, Allergies = ["nuts", "milk"] };
Dojo.Check("the Guid id is set when added", dojoGuest.Id != Guid.Empty, "Id is still empty after Add");
Dojo.Throws<DbUpdateException>("a second guest with the same email is refused", () => dojoDb.SaveChanges());
Dojo.Eq("the allergies come back", new List<string> { "nuts", "milk" }, dojoAna.Allergies);
Dojo.Eq("no allergies come back as an empty list", 0, dojoDb.Guests.Single(g => g.Name == "Ben").Allergies.Count);
dojoCmd.CommandText = "SELECT Allergies FROM Guests WHERE Name = 'Ana'";
hints: `[Owned]` on `Address`, and a `Guest.Home` property of that type.

steps.title: The night audit
prompt: Add two methods at the **top** of your code:
- `List<string> RoomsOnFloor(HotelDb db, int floor, RoomKind kind)`: the room numbers of that kind on that floor, in order.
- `Dictionary<string, int> GuestsByCountry(HotelDb db)`: how many guests live in each country (from their owned `Home` address).
Both must be answered by the database: `Where`, `OrderBy`, `GroupBy` on the `DbSet`, then a final `ToList` or `ToDictionary`.
starter: List<string> RoomsOnFloor(HotelDb db, int floor, RoomKind kind) => [];
public Address Home { get; set; } = new();
protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=hotel.db");
solution: List<string> RoomsOnFloor(HotelDb db, int floor, RoomKind kind) =>
db.Rooms.Where(r => r.Floor == floor && r.Kind == kind).OrderBy(r => r.Number).Select(r => r.Number).ToList();
db.Guests.GroupBy(g => g.Home.Country).Select(g => new { g.Key, Count = g.Count() }).ToDictionary(x => x.Key, x => x.Count);
public Address Home { get; set; } = new();
protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=hotel.db");
template: new Room { Number = "203", Kind = RoomKind.Double, Floor = 2, NightlyCents = 9000 },
new Room { Number = "201", Kind = RoomKind.Double, Floor = 2, NightlyCents = 9000 },
new Room { Number = "202", Kind = RoomKind.Suite, Floor = 2, NightlyCents = 20000 },
new Room { Number = "101", Kind = RoomKind.Double, Floor = 1, NightlyCents = 8000 });
new Guest { Name = "Ana", Email = "a@x", Home = new Address { Country = "UG" } },
new Guest { Name = "Ben", Email = "b@x", Home = new Address { Country = "KE" } },
new Guest { Name = "Cy", Email = "c@x", Home = new Address { Country = "UG" } });
Dojo.Eq("doubles on floor 2", new List<string> { "201", "203" }, RoomsOnFloor(dojoDb, 2, RoomKind.Double));
Dojo.Eq("suites on floor 1", new List<string>(), RoomsOnFloor(dojoDb, 1, RoomKind.Suite));
Dojo.Eq("guests by country", "KE=1,UG=2", string.Join(",", dojoByCountry.OrderBy(kv => kv.Key).Select(kv => kv.Key + "=" + kv.Value)));

forbid.message: Lets the database filter and group (no ToList before Where or GroupBy)

hints: Owned properties can be used in queries: `g.Home.Country`.
`GroupBy(g => g.Home.Country).Select(g => new { g.Key, Count = g.Count() })`, then `ToDictionary`.
